newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER THREATENS TO BE TOUGHER MASTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER THREATENS TO BE TOUGHER MASTER.

text.p: Bayern Munich chairman Franz Beckenbauer has warned his team he is going to become a much tougher master to please for the rest of the season.

Third-placed Bayern, one point behind leaders VfB Stuttgart, have three games to go before the Bundesliga takes its two-month winter break, starting with a home game against struggling Hansa Rostock on Saturday.

Former World Cup-winning captain and coach Beckenbauer said he knows preparations for the first half of the season were difficult because many of the Bayern players were involved in Germany's Euro 96 triumph.
But once the winter break is over in February, the "Kaiser" wants Bayern's expensive team to pay a lot more dividends.
"Bayern must produce more in the second half of the season. We will not be happy with our present standard then," former Bayern player Beckenbauer said.

"Because of Euro 96 I can understand what has happened until now. But when we return after the break we have to look at new horizons. We must be near the top spot before the break. And afterwards we have to attack. There will be no more excuses."
Bayern have won the German championship a record 13 times but they have only won the Bundesliga twice in the 1990s.
In recent seasons Beckenbauer has bought internationals such as Juergen Klinsmann and midfielder Mario Basler with the hope of taking on the best in Europe.

But, as defending champions, the Bavarians made a disappointing early exit from the UEFA Cup. Beckenbauer is determined to make sure the club is represented in the lucrative European Cup Champions' League next season.
"I see a lot of international football and see quite a few teams with big names who are not doing any better than we are," he said.
"Milan and Juventus have their weaknesses. We are still a bit behind them but, when we have all our players, we can catch up a lot."
Last season Rostock beat Bayern 1-0 in Munich's Olympic stadium but the former East German club are bottom of the table at the moment and have lost their last four away matches.

Bayern, who need a victory before they travel to Stuttgart for a fascinating clash next weekend, will be without Germany's most capped player Lothar Matthaeus, who is suspended. Euro 96 midfielder Mehmet Scholl is still struggling with an ankle injury.
Stuttgart, who are level on points with second-placed Bayer Leverkusen at the top, also take on a relegation-threatened team in Duisburg on Sunday evening. Leverkusen travel to St. Pauli on Saturday.
